at narre.explanation: "At narre" means "to fool or trick". To say someone tricked you, say: "Hun narrede os alle" (She fooled us all). Do not mix it up with "at snyde" (to cheat). For example, "Han snyder i kortspil" (He cheats at cards).

sentence.da: Han forsøgte at **narre** mig med et falsk navn.
sentence.en: He tried to fool me with a fake name.

at navngive.explanation: "At navngive" means "to name", as in giving something a name. It is built from "et navn" (a name) and "at give" (to give). To say what someone is called, use "at hedde" (to be called): "Hun hedder Anna" (Her name is Anna).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **navngive** den nye art efter hende.
sentence.en: The researchers want to name the new species after her.

at nedbryde.explanation: "At nedbryde" means "to break down", as in splitting into smaller parts. It is built from "ned" (down) and "at bryde" (to break). To say living things split waste into smaller parts, say: "Bakterier nedbryder affald" (Bacteria break down waste). To say you remove an obstacle, use it too: "at nedbryde barrierer" (to break down barriers).

sentence.da: Svampe hjælper med at **nedbryde** døde blade i skoven.
sentence.en: Fungi help break down dead leaves in the forest.

at nedkæmpe.explanation: "At nedkæmpe" means "to defeat or suppress". It is built from "ned" (down) and "at kæmpe" (to fight). To say soldiers put down a rebellion, say: "Soldaterne nedkæmper oprøret" (The soldiers put down the rebellion).

sentence.da: Politiet skal **nedkæmpe** den voksende kriminalitet i området.
sentence.en: The police must bring the growing crime in the area under control.

at nedlægge.explanation: "At nedlægge" means "to shut down or lay down". It is built from "ned" (down) and "at lægge" (to lay). To say a service is closed for good, say: "nedlægge en buslinje" (shut down a bus line). To say you place flowers in memory of someone, say: "nedlægge en krans" (lay a wreath).

forms.en: I have shut down / laid down

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **nedlægge** den lille skole, fordi der er for få børn.
sentence.en: The city will shut down the small school because there are too few children.

at nedsætte.explanation: "At nedsætte" means "to reduce". It is built from "ned" (down) and "at sætte" (to put). To say you drive more slowly, say: "nedsætte farten" (reduce speed). When you form a new group, it means "to set up": "nedsætte en arbejdsgruppe" (set up a working group).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **nedsætte** priserne på alle jakker.
sentence.en: The store will reduce the prices on all jackets.

at nedtone.explanation: "At nedtone" means "to downplay". It is built from "ned" (down) and "tone" (tone), like turning the volume down. To say someone made a problem sound small, say: "Chefen nedtonede problemet" (The boss downplayed the problem).

sentence.da: Man bør ikke **nedtone** faren, når børn leger ved vandet.
sentence.en: You should not downplay the danger when children play by the water.

at nikke.explanation: "At nikke" means "to nod". To say someone shook their head, use "at ryste på hovedet" (to shake your head): "Han rystede på hovedet" (He shook his head).

sentence.da: Hun begyndte at **nikke**, da han forklarede planen.
sentence.en: She began to nod when he explained the plan.

at nippe.explanation: "At nippe" means "to sip". To say what you sip, add "til" (to) before it: "nippe til teen" (sip the tea).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **nippe** til vinen, for jeg skal køre.
sentence.en: I will just sip the wine because I have to drive.

at notere.explanation: "At notere" means "to note down". It comes from "en note" (a note).

sentence.da: Kan du **notere** mit telefonnummer?
sentence.en: Can you note down my phone number?

at nusse.explanation: "At nusse" means "to cuddle or stroke". Do not mix it up with "at kramme" (to hug). To say you squeeze someone in your arms, use "at kramme": "Jeg krammer min mormor" (I hug my grandmother).

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **nusse** den lille hvalp.
sentence.en: The children would like to cuddle the little puppy.

at nyde.explanation: "At nyde" means "to enjoy". To say you enjoy a meal, put the meal after the verb: "Vi nyder middagen" (We are enjoying the dinner).

sentence.da: Vi vil **nyde** solen i parken i dag.
sentence.en: We want to enjoy the sun in the park today.

at nyse.explanation: "At nyse" means "to sneeze". The noun for one sneeze is "et nys". For example, "Der kom et højt nys" (There came a loud sneeze).

sentence.da: Jeg er forkølet og må **nyse** hele tiden.
sentence.en: I have a cold and have to sneeze all the time.

at nytte.explanation: "At nytte" means "to be of use". To say something is no use, add "ikke" (not): "Det nytter ikke" (It is no use). To ask whether something helps, say: "Nytter det noget?" (Does it do any good?)

sentence.da: Det vil ikke **nytte** at råbe til ham.
sentence.en: It will not help to shout at him.

at nå.explanation: "At nå" means "to reach or make it". To say you got somewhere, use the place after it: "Vi nåede hjem" (We got home). To say you were not in time, add "det" (it): "Jeg nåede det ikke" (I did not make it).

sentence.da: Jeg må løbe for at **nå** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to run to catch the bus.

at nå det.explanation: "At nå det" means "to make it". To ask whether you will be in time, say: "Tror du, vi når det?" (Do you think we will make it?) When you name the thing you reach, leave out "det" (it): "Jeg nåede bussen" (I caught the bus).

sentence.da: Toget går om fem minutter, men vi kan **nå det**.
sentence.en: The train leaves in five minutes, but we can make it.

at nå toget.explanation: "At nå toget" means "to catch the train". It is "at nå" (to reach) with "toget" (the train). To say you were too late, add "ikke" (not) after the verb: "Jeg nåede ikke toget" (I missed the train).

sentence.da: Vi skal løbe for at **nå toget**.
sentence.en: We have to run to catch the train.

at nægte.explanation: "At nægte" means "to refuse". To say someone will not do something, add "at" (to) and the action: "Han nægter at komme" (He refuses to come). When someone says a thing is not true, it means "to deny": "Hun nægter, at hun tog den" (She denies that she took it).

sentence.da: Du kan **nægte** at svare.
sentence.en: You can refuse to answer.

at nærme sig.explanation: "At nærme sig" means "to approach". It comes from "nær" (close). To say you come closer to a place, name the place after the verb: "Vi nærmer os byen" (We are approaching the city). To say a date is coming, use it for time: "Julen nærmer sig" (Christmas is getting closer).

sentence.da: Katten vil **nærme sig** fuglen langsomt.
sentence.en: The cat will approach the bird slowly.

at nævne.explanation: "At nævne" means "to mention". It is related to "et navn" (a name), since you name something when you mention it. To say someone did not mention something, say: "Hun nævnte det ikke" (She did not mention it).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nævne** det for ham.
sentence.en: You must not mention it to him.

at nøjes med.explanation: "At nøjes med" means "to make do with". To say you accept a smaller option, put it after "med" (with): "Vi nøjes med en lille bil" (We make do with a small car).

sentence.da: Vi må **nøjes med** én kop kaffe i dag.
sentence.en: We must make do with one cup of coffee today.

at nøle.explanation: "At nøle" means "to hesitate". To say what you hesitate to do, add "med at" (with to) and the verb: "Han nølede med at svare" (He hesitated to answer).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nøle**, hvis du har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not hesitate if you need help.

en nabo.explanation: "En nabo" means "a neighbor". To talk about a woman next door, use the same word as for a man: "Min nabo er en sød dame" (My neighbor is a nice lady).

sentence.da: Min **nabo** bor ved siden af.
sentence.en: My neighbor lives next door.

en nakke.explanation: "En nakke" means "a nape". To say the back of your neck hurts, say: "Jeg har ondt i nakken" (My nape hurts). Do not mix it up with "en hals" (a neck or throat). For example, "Jeg har ondt i halsen" (I have a sore throat).

sentence.da: Jeg har en stiv **nakke** efter en lang bilkørsel.
sentence.en: I have a stiff neck after a long drive.

en narkoman.explanation: "En narkoman" means "a drug addict". A similar word is "en stofmisbruger" (a drug abuser). For example, "Han er stofmisbruger" (He is a drug abuser).

sentence.da: En **narkoman** er afhængig af stoffer og har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: A drug addict is dependent on drugs and needs help.

en nat.explanation: "En nat" means "a night". To say at night, use "om natten" (at night): "Jeg sover om natten" (I sleep at night). To say tonight, use "i nat" (tonight): "Jeg sover hos dig i nat" (I am sleeping at your place tonight). To wish someone a good night, say: "Godnat, sov godt" (Good night, sleep well).

sentence.da: En **nat** varer fra aften til morgen.
sentence.en: A night lasts from evening to morning.

en nation.explanation: "En nation" means "a nation". To say the United Nations in full, use the plural: "De Forenede Nationer" (the United Nations). Its short form is "FN".

sentence.da: Danmark er en lille **nation** i Europa.
sentence.en: Denmark is a small nation in Europe.

en nationalbank.explanation: "En nationalbank" means "a central bank". It is built from "national" (national) and "en bank" (a bank).

sentence.da: Landets **nationalbank** bestemmer renten og udsteder pengene.
sentence.en: The country's central bank sets the interest rate and issues the money.

en nationalitet.explanation: "En nationalitet" means "a nationality". To ask someone, say: "Hvilken nationalitet har du?" (What nationality are you?) To answer, say: "Jeg er dansk" (I am Danish).

sentence.da: Min mand har en anden **nationalitet** end mig.
sentence.en: My husband has a different nationality than me.

en nationalpark.explanation: "En nationalpark" means "a national park". It is built from "national" (national) and "en park" (a park). To say a place is Denmark's first one, say: "Nationalpark Thy var Danmarks første nationalpark" (Nationalpark Thy was Denmark's first national park).

sentence.da: I en **nationalpark** beskytter man dyr og natur.
sentence.en: In a national park, animals and nature are protected.

en natklub.explanation: "En natklub" means "a nightclub". It is built from "nat" (night) and "en klub" (a club). The same "nat" is in "en natkjole" (a nightgown).

sentence.da: Vi danser hele natten i en **natklub** i byen.
sentence.en: We dance all night in a nightclub in town.

en natlampe.explanation: "En natlampe" means "a bedside lamp". It is built from "nat" (night) and "en lampe" (a lamp). The same "nat" is in "en natkjole" (a nightgown).

sentence.da: Jeg har en lille **natlampe** ved min seng.
sentence.en: I have a small bedside lamp by my bed.

en nattesøvn.explanation: "En nattesøvn" means "a night's sleep". To say you need a good night's sleep, put "god" (good) in front: "Jeg trænger til en god nattesøvn" (I need a good night's sleep).

sentence.da: De fleste voksne har brug for syv timers **nattesøvn**.
sentence.en: Most adults need seven hours of sleep a night.

en naturkatastrofe.explanation: "En naturkatastrofe" means "a natural disaster". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "en katastrofe" (a disaster). To say a place was hit by one, say: "Området blev ramt af en naturkatastrofe" (The area was hit by a natural disaster).

sentence.da: En oversvømmelse eller et jordskælv kan være en **naturkatastrofe**.
sentence.en: A flood or an earthquake can be a natural disaster.

en naturvejleder.explanation: "En naturvejleder" means "a nature guide". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "en vejleder" (an adviser). To say you go on a walk led by one, say: "Vi går en tur med en naturvejleder" (We go for a walk with a nature guide).

sentence.da: En **naturvejleder** fortæller om dyrene og planterne i skoven.
sentence.en: A nature guide tells about the animals and plants in the forest.

en navle.explanation: "En navle" means "a navel". The same "navle" is the start of "en navlestreng" (an umbilical cord). Do not mix it up with "et nav" (a hub), the middle part of a wheel. For example, "Hjulet har et nav" (The wheel has a hub).

sentence.da: Barnet har en lille **navle** midt på maven.
sentence.en: The child has a small navel in the middle of the stomach.

en navngivning.explanation: "En navngivning" means "a naming". It comes from the verb "at navngive" (to name). To talk about naming a baby, say: "navngivningen af barnet" (the naming of the child).

sentence.da: Ved **navngivning** af en ny art bruger forskere ofte latin.
sentence.en: When naming a new species, scientists often use Latin.

en nederdel.explanation: "En nederdel" means "a skirt". It is built from "ned" (down) and "en del" (a part), so it literally means "a lower part".

sentence.da: Hun tager en **nederdel** på, ikke bukser.
sentence.en: She puts on a skirt, not pants.

en nedgang.explanation: "En nedgang" means "a decline". To say an amount went down, use "i" (in) after it: "en nedgang i priserne" (a decline in prices). When you talk about a way down to a lower place, it means "a way down": "Nedgangen til metroen er her" (The way down to the metro is here).

sentence.da: Der var en **nedgang** i antallet af turister i år.
sentence.en: There was a decline in the number of tourists this year.

en nedskæring.explanation: "En nedskæring" means "a cutback". It comes from "at skære ned" (to cut back). To say cutbacks are carried out, use "at gennemføre" (to carry out): "Kommunen gennemfører nedskæringer på skolerne" (The municipality is carrying out cutbacks at the schools).

sentence.da: Skolen står over for en stor **nedskæring** i budgettet.
sentence.en: The school faces a big cutback in its budget.

en negl.explanation: "En negl" means "a nail", as in the nail on a finger or toe. To talk about a nail you hit with a hammer, use "et søm" (a nail): "Jeg slår et søm i væggen" (I hammer a nail into the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg har knækket en **negl** på min finger.
sentence.en: I have broken a nail on my finger.

en neglesalon.explanation: "En neglesalon" means "a nail salon". It is built from "negle" (nails) and "en salon" (a salon). To say you are going there to get your nails done, say: "Jeg skal have lavet negle" (I am getting my nails done).

sentence.da: I en **neglesalon** kan man få lakeret sine negle.
sentence.en: In a nail salon you can get your nails polished.

en nerve.explanation: "En nerve" means "a nerve". To say something annoys you, use "at gå én på nerverne" (to get on someone's nerves): "Støjen går mig på nerverne" (The noise gets on my nerves).

sentence.da: En **nerve** sender signaler fra hjernen til musklerne.
sentence.en: A nerve sends signals from the brain to the muscles.

en nevø.explanation: "En nevø" means "a nephew". To say a niece instead, use "en niece" (a niece): "Min niece er fem år" (My niece is five years old).

sentence.da: Min **nevø** kalder mig onkel.
sentence.en: My nephew calls me uncle.

en niece.explanation: "En niece" means "a niece". To say a nephew instead, use "en nevø" (a nephew): "Min nevø er syv år" (My nephew is seven years old).

sentence.da: Min **niece** kalder mig tante.
sentence.en: My niece calls me aunt.

en nisse.explanation: "En nisse" means "a Christmas elf". In Danish folklore, "nissen" is a small creature in a red cap who plays tricks if people do not treat him well. At Christmas, Danish children put out "risengrød" (rice porridge) for him.

sentence.da: Børnene satte risengrød frem til den lille **nisse**.
sentence.en: The children put out rice porridge for the little elf.

en nordmand.explanation: "En nordmand" means "a Norwegian". It is built from "nord" (north) and "en mand" (a man). To name the country, use "Norge" (Norway): "Han kommer fra Norge" (He comes from Norway).

sentence.da: Hun er **nordmand** og bor i Oslo.
sentence.en: She is Norwegian and lives in Oslo.

en norm.explanation: "En norm" means "a norm". To say something is the normal way to behave, use "normen" (the norm): "Det er normen, at man siger tak for mad" (It is the norm to say thanks for the food).

sentence.da: I Danmark er det en **norm** at komme til tiden.
sentence.en: In Denmark it is a norm to arrive on time.

en note.explanation: "En note" means "a note". To say you write things down while someone speaks, use "at tage noter" (to take notes): "Jeg tager noter i timen" (I take notes in class).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en **note** på køleskabet.
sentence.en: I put a note on the fridge.

en notesbog.explanation: "En notesbog" means "a notebook". It ends in "bog" (book), like "en ordbog" (a dictionary) and "en lærebog" (a textbook).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver nye ord i min **notesbog**.
sentence.en: I write new words in my notebook.

en novelle.explanation: "En novelle" means "a short story". To say someone has written one, say: "Hun har skrevet en novelle om sin barndom" (She has written a short story about her childhood). Do not mix it up with "en roman" (a novel), a long book. For example, "Romanen har 400 sider" (The novel has 400 pages).

sentence.da: En **novelle** er meget kortere end en roman.
sentence.en: A short story is much shorter than a novel.

en nuance.explanation: "En nuance" means "a nuance". When you talk about color, it means "a shade": "en nuance af blå" (a shade of blue).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **nuance** i betydningen af de to ord.
sentence.en: There is a small nuance in the meaning of the two words.

en nummerplade.explanation: "En nummerplade" means "a license plate". It is built from "nummer" (number) and "en plade" (a plate). "Plade" also means "record", as in "en vinylplade" (a vinyl record).

sentence.da: Hvad er nummeret på din **nummerplade**?
sentence.en: What is the number on your license plate?

en nyhed.explanation: "En nyhed" means "a piece of news". To talk about one item of news, say: "Det er en dårlig nyhed" (That is bad news). To talk about the news on TV or radio, use "nyhederne" (the news): "Nyhederne begynder nu" (The news is starting now).

sentence.da: Jeg har en god **nyhed** til dig.
sentence.en: I have good news for you.

en nyhedsside.explanation: "En nyhedsside" means "a news site". It is built from "nyhed" (a piece of news) and "en side" (a page or a site). To talk about one page in a printed newspaper, use "en avisside" (a newspaper page): "Jeg læser en avisside" (I am reading a newspaper page).

sentence.da: På en **nyhedsside** kan man følge med i dagens begivenheder.
sentence.en: On a news site you can keep up with the events of the day.

en nyhedsudsendelse.explanation: "En nyhedsudsendelse" means "a news broadcast". It is built from "nyhed" (a piece of news) and "en udsendelse" (a broadcast). To say you watch it in the evening, say: "Jeg ser nyhedsudsendelsen om aftenen" (I watch the news broadcast in the evening).

sentence.da: I en **nyhedsudsendelse** hører man, hvad der er sket i dag.
sentence.en: In a news broadcast you hear what has happened today.

en nyhedsvært.explanation: "En nyhedsvært" means "a news anchor". It is built from "nyhed" (a piece of news) and "en vært" (a host). When you talk about the host of a party, use "vært" alone: "Værten byder gæsterne velkommen" (The host welcomes the guests).

sentence.da: En **nyhedsvært** præsenterer dagens vigtigste historier i studiet.
sentence.en: A news anchor presents the day's most important stories in the studio.

en nyre.explanation: "En nyre" means "a kidney". The same "nyre" is in "en nyresten" (a kidney stone). To say someone gave a kidney to another person, say: "Han har doneret en nyre til sin bror" (He has donated a kidney to his brother).

sentence.da: En **nyre** renser blodet og laver urin.
sentence.en: A kidney cleans the blood and makes urine.

en nytårskur.explanation: "En nytårskur" means "a New Year's reception". It is a Danish custom for a company or an organization to invite guests to one in early January, with drinks and short talks, to wish each other a happy new year.

sentence.da: Firmaet inviterer alle kunder til sin årlige **nytårskur** i januar.
sentence.en: The company invites all customers to its annual New Year's reception in January.

en nål.explanation: "En nål" means "a needle". A very common pair is "nål og tråd" (needle and thread). For example, "Kan jeg låne nål og tråd?" (Can I borrow a needle and thread?).

sentence.da: Lægen stikker en **nål** i min arm.
sentence.en: The doctor sticks a needle in my arm.

en næse.explanation: "En næse" means "a nose". To say someone has a good feel for something, use "at have næse for noget" (literally, to have a nose for something): "Hun har næse for gode tilbud" (She has a nose for good deals).

sentence.da: Jeg kan lugte blomsten med min **næse**.
sentence.en: I can smell the flower with my nose.

en næsespray.explanation: "En næsespray" means "a nasal spray". It is built from "næse" (nose) and "en spray" (a spray). The same "spray" is in "en hårspray" (a hairspray).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **næsespray**, når næsen er tilstoppet.
sentence.en: I use nasal spray when my nose is blocked.

en nød.explanation: "En nød" means "a nut". When you talk about being in danger or great need, it also means "distress": "Han er i nød" (He is in distress).

sentence.da: Egernet gemmer en **nød** til vinteren.
sentence.en: The squirrel saves a nut for the winter.

en nøddeallergi.explanation: "En nøddeallergi" means "a nut allergy". It is built from "nødder" (nuts) and "en allergi" (an allergy). To read the warning on a food package, look for: "Kan indeholde spor af nødder" (May contain traces of nuts).

sentence.da: Han har **nøddeallergi** og må ikke spise mandler.
sentence.en: He has a nut allergy and must not eat almonds.

en nødsituation.explanation: "En nødsituation" means "an emergency". It is built from "nød" (distress) and "en situation" (a situation). The same "nød" is in "en nødudgang" (an emergency exit) and "et nødopkald" (an emergency call).

sentence.da: Ring til 112, når der er en **nødsituation**.
sentence.en: Call 112 when there is an emergency.

en nødudgang.explanation: "En nødudgang" means "an emergency exit". It is built from "nød" (distress) and "en udgang" (an exit). To tell people where to go in danger, say: "Brug nødudgangen" (Use the emergency exit).

sentence.da: Døren er en **nødudgang**, og den må ikke låses.
sentence.en: The door is an emergency exit and must not be locked.

en nødvendighed.explanation: "En nødvendighed" means "a necessity". It comes from the adjective "nødvendig" (necessary). To say something is necessary, use "nødvendigt": "Det er nødvendigt at have pas" (It is necessary to have a passport).

sentence.da: Rent vand er en **nødvendighed**, men ikke alle har det.
sentence.en: Clean water is a necessity, but not everyone has it.

en nøgle.explanation: "En nøgle" means "a key". To say which door a key belongs to, use "til" (to) after it: "nøglen til din lejlighed" (the key to your apartment).

sentence.da: Jeg åbner døren med min **nøgle**.
sentence.en: I open the door with my key.

en nøglering.explanation: "En nøglering" means "a key ring". It is built from "nøgle" (key) and "en ring" (a ring). To say you have lost it, say: "Jeg har mistet min nøglering" (I have lost my key ring).

sentence.da: Jeg har otte nøgler på min **nøglering**.
sentence.en: I have eight keys on my key ring.

en nørd.explanation: "En nørd" means "a nerd". To say what someone is a nerd about, put the topic in front in one word: "en computernørd" (a computer nerd) and "en filmnørd" (a movie nerd).

sentence.da: Min bror er en **nørd** og elsker computere.
sentence.en: My brother is a nerd and loves computers.

et nabolag.explanation: "Et nabolag" means "a neighborhood". It comes from "en nabo" (a neighbor). To say what kind of people live close to you, say: "Der bor mange børnefamilier i vores nabolag" (Many families with children live in our neighborhood).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et rart **nabolag** nær skolen.
sentence.en: We live in a nice neighborhood near the school.

et naboskab.explanation: "Et naboskab" means "a neighborhood relationship". The ending "-skab" names a relationship, as in "et venskab" (a friendship). The people themselves are "naboer" (neighbors). For example, "Mine naboer er søde" (My neighbors are nice).

sentence.da: Et godt **naboskab** betyder, at man hjælper hinanden.
sentence.en: A good neighborhood relationship means that people help each other.

et natbord.explanation: "Et natbord" means "a nightstand". It is built from "nat" (night) and "et bord" (a table). The same "bord" is in "et skrivebord" (a desk) and "et spisebord" (a dining table).

sentence.da: Jeg har en lampe og en bog på mit **natbord**.
sentence.en: I have a lamp and a book on my nightstand.

et naturområde.explanation: "Et naturområde" means "a nature area". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "et område" (an area). The same "område" is in "et boligområde" (a residential area) and "et industriområde" (an industrial area).

sentence.da: Vi går tur i et stort **naturområde** med sø og skov.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in a large nature area with a lake and forest.

et navn.explanation: "Et navn" means "a name". To ask someone's name, say "Hvad hedder du?" (What is your name?, literally "What are you called?"). To give your own name, say: "Jeg hedder Anna" (My name is Anna).

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **navn**?
sentence.en: What is your name?

et navneord.explanation: "Et navneord" means "a noun". It is built from "navn" (name) and "et ord" (a word). Another word for it is "et substantiv" (a noun). Two examples of nouns are "en bil" (a car) and "Anna".

sentence.da: **Navneord** er ord for personer, steder og ting.
sentence.en: Nouns are words for people, places and things.

et nedbrud.explanation: "Et nedbrud" means "a crash". It is built from "ned" (down) and "et brud" (a break). The same "brud" is in "et benbrud" (a broken bone).

sentence.da: Efter et **nedbrud** skal jeg starte computeren igen.
sentence.en: After a crash, I have to start the computer again.

et nederlag.explanation: "Et nederlag" means "a defeat". To say a team or a person is beaten, use "at lide nederlag" (to suffer defeat): "Danmark led nederlag i finalen" (Denmark suffered defeat in the final).

sentence.da: Holdet tabte 5-0, og alle kaldte det et stort **nederlag**.
sentence.en: The team lost 5-0, and everyone called it a big defeat.

et net.explanation: "Et net" means "a net". When you talk about the internet, use "nettet" (the net): "Jeg søger på nettet" (I am searching on the internet).

sentence.da: Han fangede en stor fisk i sit **net**.
sentence.en: He caught a big fish in his net.

et netværk.explanation: "Et netværk" means "a network". It is built from "et net" (a net) and "et værk" (a work). To say you know many useful people, use "at have et godt netværk" (to have a good network): "Hun har et stort netværk" (She has a large network).

sentence.da: Vores computere er på det samme **netværk**.
sentence.en: Our computers are on the same network.

et nik.explanation: "Et nik" means "a nod". The verb is "at nikke" (to nod). For example, "Han nikker til mig" (He nods at me).

sentence.da: Hun svarede med et **nik** og smilede.
sentence.en: She answered with a nod and smiled.

et niveau.explanation: "Et niveau" means "a level". To say how advanced a class is, use it for the steps: "Vi har tre niveauer: begynder, mellem og avanceret" (We have three levels: beginner, intermediate and advanced). Spell the ending "-eau", as in the French word.

sentence.da: Han spiller tennis på et højt **niveau**.
sentence.en: He plays tennis at a high level.

et nummer.explanation: "Et nummer" means "a number", as in a label such as "et telefonnummer" (a phone number). To count things or give an amount, use "et tal" (a number or figure) instead: "Tre er et ulige tal" (Three is an odd number).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dit **nummer**.
sentence.en: I call your number.

et nyhedsbrev.explanation: "Et nyhedsbrev" means "a newsletter". It is built from "nyhed" (a piece of news) and "et brev" (a letter). To join the list, use "at tilmelde sig" (to sign up): "Jeg vil gerne tilmelde mig nyhedsbrevet" (I would like to sign up for the newsletter). To leave it, use "at afmelde sig fra" (to unsubscribe from): "Jeg afmelder mig fra nyhedsbrevet" (I am unsubscribing from the newsletter).

sentence.da: Butikken sender et **nyhedsbrev** med nye tilbud hver måned.
sentence.en: The store sends a newsletter with new offers every month.

et nyhedsprogram.explanation: "Et nyhedsprogram" means "a news program". The first part, "nyheds-", comes from "nyhed" (a piece of news). To say you watch one, say: "Jeg ser et nyhedsprogram hver aften" (I watch a news program every evening).

sentence.da: I et **nyhedsprogram** fortæller en vært om dagens vigtigste begivenheder.
sentence.en: In a news program, a host tells about the most important events of the day.

et nys.explanation: "Et nys" means "a sneeze". The verb is "at nyse" (to sneeze). For example, "Jeg skal nyse" (I have to sneeze).

sentence.da: Hun gav et højt **nys**, og alle kiggede på hende.
sentence.en: She gave a loud sneeze, and everyone looked at her.

et nytår.explanation: "Et nytår" means "a New Year". It is built from "ny" (new) and "et år" (a year). To wish someone a happy New Year, say: "Godt nytår!" (Happy New Year!) To say you celebrate it, use "at holde nytår" (to celebrate New Year): "Vi holder nytår hos mine forældre" (We celebrate New Year at my parents' place).

sentence.da: Ved **nytår** ser vi fyrværkeri.
sentence.en: At New Year, we watch fireworks.

et næb.explanation: "Et næb" means "a beak". The phrase "Hold næb!" (Shut up!, literally "Hold beak!") is rude.

sentence.da: Fuglen bruger sit **næb** til at samle mad op.
sentence.en: The bird uses its beak to pick up food.

et nødopkald.explanation: "Et nødopkald" means "an emergency call". It is built from "nød" (distress) and "et opkald" (a call). In Denmark, the number to call for help is "112".

sentence.da: Man foretager et **nødopkald** til 112, når nogen er i fare.
sentence.en: You make an emergency call to 112 when someone is in danger.

et nødstilfælde.explanation: "Et nødstilfælde" means "an emergency". It is built from "nød" (distress) and "et tilfælde" (a case). To say what to do if there is an emergency, use "i" (in) before it: "Brug døren i nødstilfælde" (Use the door in an emergency).

sentence.da: Når nogen holder op med at trække vejret, er det et **nødstilfælde**.
sentence.en: When someone stops breathing, it is an emergency.

et nøglekort.explanation: "Et nøglekort" means "a key card". It is built from "nøgle" (key) and "et kort" (a card). To tell someone how to open the door with it, say: "Hold nøglekortet op til læseren" (Hold the key card up to the reader).

sentence.da: Hotellet giver mig et **nøglekort** til værelset.
sentence.en: The hotel gives me a key card for the room.

naiv.explanation: "Naiv" means "naive". After "det" (it, that), add "t" to the word: "Det var naivt at tro på ham" (It was naive to believe him).

sentence.da: Jeg var **naiv**, da jeg stolede på ham.
sentence.en: I was naive when I trusted him.

narkose.explanation: "En narkose" means "anesthesia", as in the deep sleep for an operation. To say a patient is under it, use "i narkose" (under anesthesia). To numb only one spot, use "en lokalbedøvelse" (a local anesthetic): "Tandlægen giver mig lokalbedøvelse" (The dentist gives me a local anesthetic).

sentence.da: Hun lå i **narkose** under hele operationen.
sentence.en: She was under anesthesia during the whole operation.

narkotika.explanation: "Narkotika" means "narcotics". To say someone takes drugs, use it without an article: "Han tager narkotika" (He takes drugs).

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at sælge **narkotika**.
sentence.en: It is illegal to sell narcotics.

national.explanation: "National" means "national". To say something belongs to one town only, use "lokal" (local): "en lokal avis" (a local paper). With an "et" word, add "t" to "national": "et nationalt symbol" (a national symbol).

sentence.da: Fodbold er en **national** passion i mange lande.
sentence.en: Soccer is a national passion in many countries.

nato.explanation: "NATO" means "NATO". To join it to another word, add a hyphen: "et NATO-møde" (a NATO meeting).

sentence.da: Danmark har været med i **NATO** i mange år.
sentence.en: Denmark has been in NATO for many years.

natur.explanation: "Natur" means "nature". It has no article before it. To say you spend time outdoors, say "i naturen" (in nature): "Vi går en tur i naturen" (We go for a walk in nature).

sentence.da: Danmark har smuk **natur**.
sentence.en: Denmark has beautiful nature.

naturgas.explanation: "En naturgas" means "natural gas". It is built from "natur" (nature) and "en gas" (a gas). To say a house is heated with it, say: "Vi fyrer med naturgas" (We heat with natural gas).

forms.en: The price of natural gas is rising

sentence.da: Mange huse bliver opvarmet med **naturgas**.
sentence.en: Many houses are heated with natural gas.

naturlig.explanation: "Naturlig" means "natural". To say something is normal and expected, add "t" after "det": "Det er helt naturligt at være nervøs" (It is completely natural to be nervous). To say something comes from the world as it is, not made by people, use it before a plural noun: "naturlige materialer" (natural materials).

sentence.da: Hun har en **naturlig** evne til at tegne.
sentence.en: She has a natural ability to draw.

naturligvis.explanation: "Naturligvis" means "of course". The ending "-vis" is also in "heldigvis" (luckily). To answer a question with yes, say it as a reply: "Kan du hjælpe?" "Naturligvis!" (Can you help? Of course!)

sentence.da: **Naturligvis** hjælper jeg dig i morgen.
sentence.en: Of course I will help you tomorrow.

navnemåde.explanation: "En navnemåde" means "an infinitive". It is built from "et navn" (a name) and "en måde" (a way), because this form only names the action. In Danish it has "at" (to) in front. For example, "at spise" (to eat).

sentence.da: Verbet at gå står i **navnemåde**.
sentence.en: The verb at gå is in its plain form.

navnlig.explanation: "Navnlig" means "especially". It is built from "navn" (name) and the ending "-lig". To point out one example from a group, say: "Jeg kan lide sport, navnlig fodbold" (I like sports, especially soccer).

sentence.da: Mange kan lide frugt, **navnlig** æbler.
sentence.en: Many people like fruit, especially apples.

ned.explanation: "Ned" means "down". To tell someone to move to a lower place, say: "Kom ned!" (Come down!) To say where a person already is down there, use "nede" (down there): "Han er nede i kælderen" (He is down in the cellar).

sentence.da: Elevatoren går op og **ned**.
sentence.en: The elevator goes up and down.

nedad.explanation: "Nedad" means "downward". It is built from "ned" (down) and "ad" (along). To say prices are falling, say: "Priserne går nedad" (Prices are going downward).

sentence.da: Vandet løber **nedad**, fordi vejen hælder.
sentence.en: The water runs downward because the road slopes.

nedenunder.explanation: "Nedenunder" means "downstairs". It is built from "neden" (below) and "under" (under). To say a room is on the floor above instead, use "ovenpå" (upstairs): "Soveværelset er ovenpå" (The bedroom is upstairs).

sentence.da: Vores nabo bor **nedenunder**.
sentence.en: Our neighbor lives downstairs.

nedslående.explanation: "Nedslående" means "disheartening". To describe bad news, use it before the noun: "nedslående nyheder" (disheartening news). To say a person feels low, use "nedtrykt" (downcast): "Hun er nedtrykt" (She is downcast).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **nedslående**, men vi giver ikke op.
sentence.en: The result was disheartening, but we are not giving up.

nedtrykt.explanation: "Nedtrykt" means "downcast". It is built from "ned" (down) and "trykt" (pressed), so it literally means "pressed down". To say someone seems low in spirit, say: "Hun virker nedtrykt i dag" (She seems downcast today).

sentence.da: Efter nyheden var han **nedtrykt** i flere dage.
sentence.en: After the news he was downcast for several days.

negativ.explanation: "Negativ" means "negative". To say a medical test found nothing, use it for the result: "Testen var negativ" (The test was negative).

sentence.da: Han har en meget **negativ** holdning.
sentence.en: He has a very negative attitude.

neglelak.explanation: "Neglelak" means "nail polish". It is built from "negle" (nails) and "en lak" (a lacquer). To take it off, you need "neglelakfjerner" (nail polish remover): "Har du neglelakfjerner?" (Do you have nail polish remover?)

sentence.da: Hun har rød **neglelak** på fingrene.
sentence.en: She has red nail polish on her fingers.

nej.explanation: "Nej" means "no". When you are surprised or impressed, it also means "oh!": "Nej, hvor er det flot!" (Oh, how beautiful!) To answer yes to a question with "ikke" (not), say "jo" (yes) instead of "ja": "Kan du ikke komme?" "Jo, det kan jeg." (Can't you come? Yes, I can.)

sentence.da: Vil du have kaffe? **Nej**, tak.
sentence.en: Do you want coffee? No, thank you.

nem.explanation: "Nem" means "easy". To say something is easy to do, use "nem at" (easy to) before the verb: "Appen er nem at bruge" (The app is easy to use). To say a task is hard instead, use "svær" (hard): "en svær opgave" (a hard task).

sentence.da: En **nem** opskrift tager kun ti minutter.
sentence.en: An easy recipe takes only ten minutes.

nemlig.explanation: "Nemlig" means "exactly". To agree with someone, say it as a reply: "Er du træt?" "Nemlig!" (Are you tired? Exactly!) When you give a reason inside a sentence, it means "you see": "Jeg bliver hjemme, jeg er nemlig syg" (I am staying home, I am sick, you see).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke komme, jeg er **nemlig** syg.
sentence.en: I cannot come, I am sick, you see.

nemt.explanation: "Nemt" means "easy". To say how something is done, it means "easily": "Han vinder nemt" (He wins easily). With an "en" word, use "nem" instead: "en nem opgave" (an easy task).

sentence.da: Det er **nemt**: to plus to er fire.
sentence.en: It is easy: two plus two is four.

nervepirrende.explanation: "Nervepirrende" means "nerve-wracking". It is built from "en nerve" (a nerve) and "pirrende" (irritating). To describe a movie that makes you tense, say: "en nervepirrende film" (a nerve-wracking movie).

sentence.da: Ventetiden før eksamensresultatet var **nervepirrende**, og jeg sov dårligt.
sentence.en: The wait before the exam result was nerve-wracking, and I slept badly.

nervøs.explanation: "Nervøs" means "nervous". To say you feel it before something important, say: "Jeg er nervøs før eksamen" (I am nervous before the exam). To say someone is calm instead, use "rolig" (calm): "Hun er helt rolig" (She is completely calm).

sentence.da: Han er **nervøs**, fordi han skal til tandlægen.
sentence.en: He is nervous because he has to go to the dentist.

nervøsitet.explanation: "En nervøsitet" means "a nervousness". It comes from "nervøs" (nervous). The ending "-itet" is also in "en aktivitet" (an activity). To say someone showed none, say: "Han viste ingen nervøsitet" (He showed no nervousness).

sentence.da: Man kan se hendes **nervøsitet**, når hun skal tale.
sentence.en: You can see her nervousness when she has to speak.

netop.explanation: "Netop" means "exactly". To agree with exactly what someone said, say it as a reply: "Netop!" (Exactly!) To say something happened a moment ago, it means "just": "Han er netop gået" (He just left).

forms.da: Det er netop, hvad jeg mente.
forms.en: That is exactly what I meant.

sentence.da: Jeg skulle **netop** til at ringe til dig.
sentence.en: I was just about to call you.

neutral.explanation: "Neutral" means "neutral". To say a country takes no side in a conflict, say: "et neutralt land" (a neutral country). To say a color goes with everything, such as gray, say: "en neutral farve" (a neutral color).

sentence.da: Dommeren skal være **neutral** og ikke holde med nogen.
sentence.en: The referee must be neutral and not support anyone.

ni.explanation: "Ni" means "nine". The same "ni" starts "nitten" (nineteen) and "niende" (ninth). To say a multiplication, say: "Tre gange ni er syvogtyve" (Three times nine is twenty-seven).

sentence.da: Efter otte kommer **ni**.
sentence.en: After eight comes nine.

niende.explanation: "Niende" means "ninth". To put things in order, use it after "den" (the): "den niende dag" (the ninth day). To say a date, use it before the month: "den niende maj" (the ninth of May).

sentence.da: Efter den ottende dag kommer den **niende** dag.
sentence.en: After the eighth day comes the ninth day.

nitten.explanation: "Nitten" means "nineteen". To say how much money you have, say: "Jeg har nitten kroner" (I have nineteen kroner).

sentence.da: Min søster er **nitten** år.
sentence.en: My sister is nineteen years old.

nogen.explanation: "Nogen" means "anyone". To say you see a person, it means "someone": "Jeg ser nogen" (I see someone). In a question, or after "ikke" (not), it also means "any". For example, "Har du nogen børn?" (Do you have any children?)

sentence.da: Der er ikke **nogen** hjemme.
sentence.en: Nobody is home.

nogenlunde.explanation: "Nogenlunde" means "reasonably". To answer "How is it going?" with "so-so", say it as a reply: "Hvordan går det?" "Nogenlunde." (How is it going? So-so.)

sentence.da: Jeg taler **nogenlunde** dansk, men jeg laver stadig fejl.
sentence.en: I speak Danish reasonably well, but I still make mistakes.

nogensinde.explanation: "Nogensinde" means "ever". To ask about your whole life, use it in a question: "Har du nogensinde været i Paris?" (Have you ever been to Paris?) To say never, use "aldrig" (never): "Jeg har aldrig været i Paris" (I have never been to Paris).

sentence.da: Har du **nogensinde** været i Norge?
sentence.en: Have you ever been to Norway?

noget.explanation: "Noget" means "something". To say you see a thing, say: "Jeg ser noget" (I see something). To say you see a person, use "nogen" (someone): "Jeg ser nogen" (I see someone). Before something you cannot count one by one, such as milk, it means "some". For example, "noget mælk" (some milk).

forms.da: Vil du have noget at spise?
forms.en: Do you want something to eat?

sentence.da: Jeg er tørstig. Har du **noget** at drikke?
sentence.en: I am thirsty. Do you have something to drink?

nogle.explanation: "Nogle" means "some", and it goes with more than one thing. For example, "Jeg har nogle venner" (I have some friends). To talk about one thing, use "en" (a): "Jeg har en ven" (I have one friend). In a question, or after "ikke" (not), use "nogen" (any): "Har du nogen venner?" (Do you have any friends?)

sentence.da: Der er **nogle** æbler på bordet.
sentence.en: There are some apples on the table.

nogle gange.explanation: "Nogle gange" means "sometimes" (literally, "some times"). To say you do something now and then, put it in the sentence: "Jeg spiser nogle gange morgenmad" (I sometimes eat breakfast). To say always, use "altid" (always): "Jeg spiser altid morgenmad" (I always eat breakfast).

sentence.da: **Nogle gange** tager jeg bussen.
sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bus.

nok.explanation: "Nok" means "enough". To say you have enough of something, say: "Jeg har nok mad" (I have enough food). To say what you guess will happen, it means "probably": "Han kommer nok" (He will probably come).

forms.en: I do not have enough time.

sentence.da: Nej tak, jeg har **nok** mad.
sentence.en: No thanks, I have enough food.

nord.explanation: "Nord" means "north". To say where something is, use "i nord" (in the north): "Skoven ligger i nord" (The forest is in the north). To say which way you are going, use "mod nord" (toward the north): "Vi kører mod nord" (We drive toward the north). The same "nord" is in "Nordjylland" (North Jutland).

sentence.da: Kompasnålen peger mod **nord**.
sentence.en: The compass needle points north.

nordamerika.explanation: "Nordamerika" means "North America". It is built from "nord" (north) and "Amerika" (America). To say where you travel to, use "til" (to): "Vi flyver til Nordamerika" (We fly to North America).

sentence.da: Hun bor i **Nordamerika**, i Canada.
sentence.en: She lives in North America, in Canada.

norden.explanation: "Norden" means "the Nordic countries". It is the name for Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland together. It comes from "nord" (north).

sentence.da: Mange rejser mellem landene i **Norden** uden pas.
sentence.en: Many people travel between the countries of the Nordic region without a passport.

nordisk.explanation: "Nordisk" means "Nordic". It comes from "nord" (north). To talk about food from this region, say: "Vi elsker nordisk mad" (We love Nordic food). "Norsk" is a different word and means "Norwegian". For example, "Han er norsk" (He is Norwegian).

sentence.da: Danmark og Sverige har en **nordisk** velfærdsmodel.
sentence.en: Denmark and Sweden have a Nordic welfare model.

nordlig.explanation: "Nordlig" means "northerly". It comes from "nord" (north). To say where in a country a place lies, add "-e" after "det" (the): "Skagen ligger i det nordlige Danmark" (Skagen is in the northern part of Denmark).

sentence.da: Vinden er **nordlig**, og det er koldt.
sentence.en: The wind is from the north, and it is cold.

nordlys.explanation: "Nordlys" means "northern lights". It takes "et". For example, "et nordlys". It is built from "nord" (north) and "lys" (light). To say you want to see them, say: "Jeg vil gerne se nordlys" (I would like to see the northern lights).

sentence.da: Vi så **nordlys** over fjorden i Norge.
sentence.en: We saw northern lights over the fjord in Norway.

nordpå.explanation: "Nordpå" means "north". It is built from "nord" (north) and "på" (on). To say a train goes in that direction, say: "Toget kører nordpå" (The train goes north). To say where a place is located, use "i nord" (in the north): "Skoven ligger i nord" (The forest lies in the north).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver **nordpå** om foråret.
sentence.en: The birds fly north in the spring.

nordsøen.explanation: "Nordsøen" means "the North Sea". It is the sea along the west coast of "Jylland" (Jutland). Danes also call this sea "Vesterhavet" (literally, "the Western Sea").

sentence.da: **Nordsøen** ligger vest for Danmark.
sentence.en: The North Sea lies west of Denmark.

norge.explanation: "Norge" means "Norway". The language is called "norsk" (Norwegian). To say you speak it, say: "Jeg taler norsk" (I speak Norwegian).

sentence.da: Min ven kommer fra **Norge** og taler norsk.
sentence.en: My friend comes from Norway and speaks Norwegian.

normal.explanation: "Normal" means "normal". To say something is nothing unusual, add "-t" after "det er" (it is): "Det er helt normalt" (That is completely normal).

sentence.da: En **normal** kropstemperatur er 37 grader.
sentence.en: A normal body temperature is 37 degrees.

norsk.explanation: "Norsk" means "Norwegian", for things from Norway. It comes from "Norge" (Norway). When you talk about the language, use it as a name: "Jeg taler norsk" (I speak Norwegian).

sentence.da: I Oslo taler man **norsk**.
sentence.en: In Oslo people speak Norwegian.

nougat.explanation: "Nougat" means "nougat". To ask whether a chocolate has it inside, say: "Er der nougat i chokoladen?" (Is there nougat in the chocolate?)

sentence.da: Man laver **nougat** af nødder og sukker.
sentence.en: You make nougat from nuts and sugar.

november.explanation: "November" means "November". To give a date, say the day first: "den første november" (the first of November).

sentence.da: Det er mørkt og gråt i **november**.
sentence.en: It is dark and gray in November.

nu.explanation: "Nu" means "now". To say something is happening at this moment, add "lige" (just) before it: "Jeg arbejder lige nu" (I am working right now).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå **nu**.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nu skal du høre.explanation: "Nu skal du høre" means "now listen", literally "now you shall hear". To start telling something, say: "Nu skal du høre, hvad der skete i går" (Now listen to what happened yesterday). To speak to several people, change "du" (you) to "I" (you all): "Nu skal I høre!" (Now listen, all of you!)

forms.da: Nu skal du høre, hvad jeg har at sige.
forms.en: Now listen to what I have to say.

sentence.da: Vent, **nu skal du høre**, jeg har en god nyhed.
sentence.en: Wait, now listen, I have good news.

nudler.explanation: "Nudler" means "noodles". To name a soup made with them, join the words: "en nudelsuppe" (a noodle soup).

sentence.da: Jeg koger **nudler** i vand.
sentence.en: I boil noodles in water.

nul.explanation: "Nul" means "zero". To give a sports score, it also means "nil": "Vi vinder to–nul" (We win two–nil).

sentence.da: Vandet bliver til is ved **nul** grader.
sentence.en: Water turns to ice at zero degrees.

nutid.explanation: "En nutid" means "a present tense". It is built from "nu" (now) and "tid" (time). To show a verb in the present tense, say: "jeg løber" (I run).

sentence.da: Sætningen Jeg spiser et æble står i **nutid**.
sentence.en: The sentence I eat an apple is in the present tense.

nutiden.explanation: "Nutiden" means "the present". It is built from "nu" (now) and "tiden" (the time). To talk about the young people of today, say: "nutidens unge" (the young people of today).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om fortiden, men vi lever i **nutiden**.
sentence.en: We learn about the past, but we live in the present.

nutildags.explanation: "Nutildags" means "nowadays". To compare today with the past, say: "Nutildags har alle en telefon" (Nowadays everyone has a phone). A spelling with three words also exists, "nu til dags", with the same meaning.

sentence.da: Før skrev vi breve, men **nutildags** skriver vi beskeder.
sentence.en: Before, we wrote letters, but nowadays we write messages.

nuttet.explanation: "Nuttet" means "cute". To say how cute something is, start with "hvor" (how): "Hvor er den nuttet!" (How cute it is!)

sentence.da: Din lille hund er så **nuttet**.
sentence.en: Your little dog is so cute.

nuvel.explanation: "Nuvel" means "very well". It is built from "nu" (now) and "vel" (well). To accept something and move on, say: "Nuvel, så gør vi det" (Very well, we will do it that way).

sentence.da: **Nuvel**, så er det aftalt, og vi mødes klokken ni.
sentence.en: Very well, then it is agreed, and we meet at nine.

nuværende.explanation: "Nuværende" means "current". It comes from "nu" (now). To talk about who runs a country now, say: "den nuværende regering" (the current government).

sentence.da: Min **nuværende** chef er sød, men min tidligere var streng.
sentence.en: My current boss is nice, but my former one was strict.

ny.explanation: "Ny" means "new". It is also part of "nytår" (New Year). To wish someone a happy New Year, say: "Godt nytår!" (Happy New Year!)

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **ny** telefon.
sentence.en: I have bought a new phone.

nyheder.explanation: "Nyheder" means "news". For one piece of news, use "en nyhed" (a piece of news): "Jeg har en god nyhed" (I have a piece of good news). To say the news is bad, Danish uses the plural: "Nyhederne er dårlige" (The news is bad).

sentence.da: Jeg læser **nyheder** i avisen hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news in the newspaper every morning.

nylig.explanation: "Nylig" means "recently". It is built from "ny" (new). It is used in the phrase "for nylig", with "for" (for) in front: "Jeg mødte hende for nylig" (I met her recently).

sentence.da: Jeg mødte hende for **nylig** i byen.
sentence.en: I met her recently in town.

nysgerrig.explanation: "Nysgerrig" means "curious", as in wanting to know things. To say what you are curious to do, add "efter at" (to): "Han er nysgerrig efter at lære mere" (He is curious to learn more). A second meaning is "nosy", as in asking too much about other people. For example, "Vær ikke så nysgerrig!" (Do not be so nosy!)

sentence.da: Min søn er **nysgerrig** og stiller mange spørgsmål.
sentence.en: My son is curious and asks many questions.

nysgerrighed.explanation: "En nysgerrighed" means "curiosity". It comes from "nysgerrig" (curious) with "-hed" added, like "-ness" in English. The same ending turns "fri" (free) into "en frihed" (a freedom).

sentence.da: Børn stiller mange spørgsmål af **nysgerrighed**.
sentence.en: Children ask many questions out of curiosity.

nytte.explanation: "En nytte" means "a use". To say something helps, use "at gøre nytte" (literally, "to do use"): "Paraplyen gjorde nytte" (The umbrella was useful). To say something is of no use, use "ingen" (no): "Det har ingen nytte" (It is of no use).

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **nytte** af min nye ordbog.
sentence.en: I get great use out of my new dictionary.

nyttig.explanation: "Nyttig" means "useful". It comes from "nytte" (use). To say a piece of advice helps, say: "Det er et nyttigt tip" (That is a useful tip).

sentence.da: Paraplyen er **nyttig**, når det regner.
sentence.en: The umbrella is useful when it rains.

nytårsaften.explanation: "Nytårsaften" means "New Year's Eve". It is built from "nytår" (new year) and "aften" (evening). On that evening the Danish monarch gives a speech on television, "nytårstalen" (the New Year's speech).

sentence.da: På **nytårsaften** siger vi "godt nytår" ved midnat.
sentence.en: On New Year's Eve we say "happy new year" at midnight.

nå.explanation: "Nå" means "oh". When you have just understood something, say: "Nå, det vidste jeg ikke!" (Oh, I did not know that!) To start a chat again, it also means "well": "Nå, hvad så?" (Well, what's up?)

sentence.da: **Nå**, nu forstår jeg det!
sentence.en: Oh, now I understand!

nå ja.explanation: "Nå ja" means "oh right". When you suddenly remember something, say it first: "Nå ja, nu husker jeg det" (Oh right, now I remember). The small word "jo" (as you know) can follow. For example, "Nå ja, det er jo tirsdag i dag" (Oh right, it is Tuesday today, you know).

forms.da: Nå ja, nu husker jeg det.

sentence.da: **Nå ja**, jeg skal jo hente børnene.
sentence.en: Oh right, I have to pick up the kids.

nå men.explanation: "Nå men" means "well then". To move a conversation on, say: "Nå men, lad os komme i gang" (Well then, let us get started). To end a conversation, say: "Nå men, jeg må videre" (Well then, I have to move on).

forms.da: Nå men, lad os komme i gang.

forms.en: Well then, I have to move on.

sentence.da: **Nå men**, nu må jeg hellere gå.
sentence.en: Well then, I had better go now.

nåde.explanation: "En nåde" means "a mercy". To say a person is merciful, use "at vise nåde" (to show mercy): "Dommeren viste nåde" (The judge showed mercy). A second meaning is "grace". For example, "af Guds nåde" (by the grace of God).

sentence.da: Fangen bad dommeren om **nåde**, men fik ingen.
sentence.en: The prisoner asked the judge for mercy, but got none.

når.explanation: "Når" means "when". For something that happens again and again or has not happened yet, use it like this: "Når det regner, bliver jeg hjemme" (When it rains, I stay home). For one time in the past, use "da" (when): "Da jeg kom hjem, var det mørkt" (When I came home, it was dark). To ask a question, use "hvornår" (when): "Hvornår kommer du?" (When are you coming?)

sentence.da: Jeg ringer, **når** jeg kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I will call when I get home.

når som helst.explanation: "Når som helst" means "anytime". To invite someone, say: "Kom når som helst" (Come anytime). To say something might happen without warning, it also means "at any moment": "Det kan regne når som helst" (It can rain at any moment).

forms.da: Jeg har tid når som helst.

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til mig **når som helst**.
sentence.en: You can call me anytime.

næppe.explanation: "Næppe" means "unlikely". To say something will probably not happen, put it after the verb: "Han kommer næppe" (He is unlikely to come). It also means "hardly". For example, "Jeg kan næppe kende ham" (I can hardly recognize him). A tiny chance is left, unlike "aldrig" (never). For another example, "Han kommer aldrig" (He never comes).

forms.en: She is unlikely to come today

sentence.da: Vi får **næppe** sne, fordi det er for varmt.
sentence.en: We are unlikely to get snow because it is too warm.

nær.explanation: "Nær" means "close". To talk about a person you are close to, put it before the noun: "en nær ven" (a close friend). To say a place is close to something, use "tæt på" (close to): "Jeg bor tæt på stationen" (I live close to the station).

sentence.da: Han er en **nær** ven af mig.
sentence.en: He is a close friend of mine.

nærig.explanation: "Nærig" means "stingy". It is not a compliment. Do not mix it up with "sparsommelig", which means "thrifty". For example, "Hun er sparsommelig og køber brugt" (She is thrifty and buys second-hand).

sentence.da: Han er **nærig** og giver aldrig drikkepenge.
sentence.en: He is stingy and never gives tips.

næringsrig.explanation: "Næringsrig" means "nutritious". It is built from "en næring" (nourishment) and "rig" (rich). To say a meal is nutritious, say: "Det er et næringsrigt måltid" (It is a nutritious meal).

sentence.da: Grønkål er **næringsrig**, fordi den indeholder meget jern.
sentence.en: Kale is nutritious because it contains a lot of iron.

nærmest.explanation: "Nærmest" means "almost". To say you have nearly finished, say: "Jeg er nærmest færdig" (I am almost done). A second meaning is "nearest". For example, "den nærmeste station" (the nearest station).

sentence.da: Opgaven var **nærmest** umulig at løse på en dag.
sentence.en: The task was almost impossible to solve in one day.

nærværende.explanation: "Nærværende" means "attentive". To say a father gives you his full attention, say: "Han er en nærværende far" (He is an attentive father). In a formal contract, "nærværende kontrakt" means "this contract".

sentence.da: Min læge er **nærværende** og lytter, når jeg taler.
sentence.en: My doctor is attentive and listens when I speak.

næseblod.explanation: "Næseblod" means "a nosebleed". It is built from "næse" (nose) and "blod" (blood). To say you have a nosebleed, leave out the article: "Jeg har næseblod" (I have a nosebleed).

sentence.da: Når man får **næseblod**, skal man læne sig frem.
sentence.en: When you get a nosebleed, you should lean forward.

næsten.explanation: "Næsten" means "almost". To say you have nearly finished, say: "Jeg er næsten færdig" (I am almost done). Do not mix it up with "næste", which means "next". For example, "næste uge" (next week).

sentence.da: Jeg er **næsten** færdig med arbejdet.
sentence.en: I am almost done with the work.

næsten aldrig.explanation: "Næsten aldrig" means "almost never". It is built from "næsten" (almost) and "aldrig" (never). Because "aldrig" already makes the sentence negative, do not add "ikke" (not). To say you rarely do something, say: "Hun spiser næsten aldrig kød" (She almost never eats meat).

sentence.da: Han kommer **næsten aldrig** for sent.
sentence.en: He almost never comes late.

nødder.explanation: "Nødder" means "nuts". To name one kind of nut, join its name to "nød": "en hasselnød" (a hazelnut) and "en valnød" (a walnut).

sentence.da: Egern elsker at spise **nødder**.
sentence.en: Squirrels love to eat nuts.

nødhjælp.explanation: "Nødhjælp" means "emergency aid". It is built from "nød" (distress) and "hjælp" (help). To say you collect money for victims of a disaster, say: "Vi samler nødhjælp ind til ofrene" (We collect emergency aid for the victims).

sentence.da: Efter jordskælvet sendte landene **nødhjælp** til området.
sentence.en: After the earthquake the countries sent emergency aid to the area.

nødig.explanation: "Nødig" means "rather not". Put it after "vil" (will, want) or "ville" (would): "Jeg vil nødig tage afsted" (I would rather not leave). To say someone else would rather not, say: "Hun ville nødig sige det" (She would rather not say it).

forms.en: I would rather not go alone.
She would rather not say it.

forms.da: Vi vil nødig komme for sent.
forms.en: We would rather not be late.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **nødig** forstyrre dig, når du arbejder.
sentence.en: I would rather not disturb you when you are working.

nødt til.explanation: "Nødt til" means "have to". When you have no choice, say "er nødt til at" before the verb: "Jeg er nødt til at gå" (I have to go). When you choose to go, say "Jeg vil gå" (I want to go) instead.

forms.da: jeg er nødt til at gå
du er nødt til at vente
vi er nødt til at tale

sentence.da: Jeg er **nødt til** at gå nu.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nødvendig.explanation: "Nødvendig" means "necessary". To say you cannot do without something, say: "Et pas er nødvendigt" (A passport is necessary). Do not mix it up with "vigtig", which means "important". For example, "Sundhed er vigtig" (Health is important).

sentence.da: Vand er **nødvendig**, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: Water is necessary when it is hot.

nødvendigvis.explanation: "Nødvendigvis" means "necessarily". It comes from "nødvendig" (necessary). To say something is not always true, put "ikke" (not) before it: "Han er ikke nødvendigvis rig" (He is not necessarily rich).

sentence.da: Den dyreste bil er ikke **nødvendigvis** den bedste.
sentence.en: The most expensive car is not necessarily the best.

nøgen.explanation: "Nøgen" means "naked". For trees, it also means "bare": "nøgne træer" (bare trees).

sentence.da: Han sprang **nøgen** i havet.
sentence.en: He jumped naked into the sea.

nøgtern.explanation: "Nøgtern" means "matter-of-fact". A second meaning is "sober", as in plain and without drama. For example, "nøgterne tal" (sober figures). To say someone has not been drinking, use "ædru" (sober): "Han er ædru" (He is sober).

sentence.da: Han gav en **nøgtern** beskrivelse af ulykken og overdrev ikke.
sentence.en: He gave a matter-of-fact description of the accident and did not exaggerate.

nøjagtig.explanation: "Nøjagtig" means "exact". A second meaning is "accurate", as in correct in every detail. For example, "Vi har brug for nøjagtige oplysninger" (We need accurate information).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **nøjagtig** måling.
sentence.en: We need an exact measurement.

nøjagtigt.explanation: "Nøjagtigt" means "exactly". It comes from "nøjagtig" (exact). To say a number is not exact, use "omtrent" (about): "Der kom omtrent tre hundrede mennesker" (About three hundred people came).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge **nøjagtigt** to hundrede gram mel.
sentence.en: You must use exactly two hundred grams of flour.

nøje.explanation: "Nøje" means "closely". To tell someone to read with full attention, say: "Læs kontrakten nøje" (Read the contract closely). To say something is not important, use it with "ikke så" (not so): "Det er ikke så nøje" (It does not matter that much).

forms.en: It does not matter that much

sentence.da: Man skal studere planen **nøje**, før man skriver under.
sentence.en: You must study the plan closely before you sign.
